assumptions.assumption: The bank is called 'Northline Bank' (interpretation of the user's suggestion 'world bank or something generic', avoiding a clash with the real World Bank Group). Trivial to change if a different fictional name is preferred.
The customer name Alex Taylor is hard-coded; the greeting reads exactly 'Hello, Alex' (agreed in round 1).
Money-in colour is a green matching the site's success/positive tone in both light and dark modes; money-out uses default text colour. Signs (+ / -) carry the meaning independently of colour.
The credit card account is modelled as a spending account: purchases show as -$X, payments as +$X, and the running balance is the amount owing (agreed in round 2).
Interest rate renders as '4.50% p.a.' (agreed in round 2).

Approximately twelve transactions per account (10–15 range) covering the last three months, all in AUD, with plausible Australian merchant descriptions (Coles, Woolworths, Bunnings, Optus, and so on).
The deep-blue palette lives in a Tailwind blue-700 / blue-800 family; specific hex values are the engineer's call so long as WCAG AA contrast holds and no ANZ hex is reproduced.

clarified_description: Turn the Pixie sandbox site into a small internet-banking demo for a fictional Australian bank, 'Northline Bank', styled to evoke a modern local internet-banking site (deep-blue primary palette, card-based accounts overview, clean typography) without reproducing any real bank's logos or trademarks. There is no sign-in; the site behaves as if a fictional customer, Alex Taylor, is signed in. The home page becomes an accounts overview showing three accounts — Everyday, Savings, and a Credit card — each with its name, a masked account number showing only the last four digits, and its balance in Australian dollars. Savings additionally shows an interest rate; Credit card shows the amount owing and the credit limit. Each account is a link to its own page at /accounts/<id>, which shows the account's details and a list of transactions newest first (date, description, signed amount, and running balance). The balance on the overview equals the balance after the newest transaction for each account. Unknown account ids fall through to the existing 404 page. Accounts and transactions come from a single data file at data/accounts.json, with about twelve realistic transactions per account. A simple header appears on every page linking to Accounts (home) and Changelog; the changelog page and its RSS feed keep working unchanged. There is no demo banner, no sign-in flow, and no transfer, payment or search functionality — those are explicitly out of scope.

constraints.detail: The Changelog page (app/changelog/page.tsx) and RSS route (app/changelog.xml/route.ts) must continue to serve their existing content and shape unchanged. Existing changelog tests must continue to pass without modification.
No full account or card number appears anywhere in the DOM, source, or public assets; only the last four digits are rendered (SEC-01 §4).
The [id] URL segment is validated against a fixed whitelist ('everyday', 'savings', 'credit-card') before use; unknown values call notFound() (SEC-01 §3 — treat outside input as data, not code).
No ANZ logos, wordmarks, or trademarked colour/tone assets are reproduced; the deep-blue palette is a distinct choice with no dependency on ANZ brand assets.
The accounts data file is read at build time via ES import; no runtime fetching.

data_changes.change: New file data/accounts.json containing three accounts (Everyday, Savings, Credit card) with ~12 realistic AUD transactions each. Balances derived so that account.balance equals the newest transaction's balance_after.

deferred_decisions: Exact hex values in the deep-blue palette — engineer picks specific shades (e.g. Tailwind blue-700 for primary, blue-800 for hover, softer variants for dark mode) so long as WCAG AA contrast holds in both themes and no ANZ trademarked hex is reproduced.
Whether transaction rows use <table> markup or a role='table' + <ul>/<li> pattern — either is fine so long as accessible names and column semantics are clear.
Whether components/AccountCard.tsx and components/TransactionList.tsx are extracted as separate files or inlined in their parent pages — granularity is engineering judgement.
Currency-formatting via Intl.NumberFormat vs a manual template — both are acceptable; Intl.NumberFormat is the boring choice and needs no dependency.
Whether the Header's active-item indicator is bold, an underline, or a coloured bar — visual detail left to the engineer.
Whether components/Footer.tsx's local formatDate is refactored to use lib/formatDate.ts in this change or left alone — expected but not required for the spec to be met.

flows.title: Account route resolution

must: The system shall render an accounts overview at the home page (/) that greets the customer as 'Hello, Alex' and lists three accounts: Everyday, Savings, and Credit card.

The system shall show, for each account on the overview, the account name, a masked account number displaying only the last four digits, and the account's balance formatted in Australian dollars (e.g. $1,234.56).
The system shall show the Savings account's interest rate on the overview as '4.50% p.a.'.
The system shall show the Credit card account's amount owing and credit limit on the overview, each formatted in Australian dollars and clearly labelled.
WHEN a visitor selects an account entry on the overview the system shall navigate to /accounts/<id> where <id> is one of 'everyday', 'savings', or 'credit-card'.
WHEN a visitor opens /accounts/<id> for a known account the system shall render the account's name, masked number, balance, and its transactions newest first.

The system shall render each transaction row with the transaction date formatted as DD MMM YYYY, a description, a signed amount (money in prefixed with '+' and money out prefixed with '-'), and the balance after the transaction in Australian dollars.
The system shall style money-in amounts with a visibly distinct colour (green) in addition to the '+' prefix so that the distinction does not rely on colour alone.
The system shall ensure that for every account the balance shown on the overview equals the balance after the newest transaction on that account's detail page.
IF a visitor opens /accounts/<id> with an id that does not match a known account THEN the system shall render the existing not-found page (app/not-found.tsx) via Next.js's notFound() helper.
The system shall load accounts and transactions from a single data file at data/accounts.json containing three accounts, each with approximately twelve transactions.
The system shall render a header on every page containing the site name 'Northline Bank' linking to /, two navigation links ('Accounts' → /, 'Changelog' → /changelog), and the existing ThemeToggle.
The system shall apply a deep-blue primary colour palette to header, links, and account-card accents through CSS variables defined in app/globals.css.

WHILE any page is being rendered the system shall keep the changelog page (/changelog) and RSS feed (/changelog.xml) functioning exactly as they do today, including sort order, filters and feed structure.
The system shall never render a full account or card number in the DOM; only the last four digits appear on any surface.
WHERE dark mode is active the system shall render the deep-blue palette with contrast-appropriate variants so that text and interactive elements remain readable (WCAG 2.1 AA).

non_functional.target: Static server render; data/accounts.json <50KB; each page contentful under 1s on modest hardware

non_functional.why_not: Demo site with no runtime dependencies; availability is that of the static host.
No runtime state, external calls or error paths beyond the existing 404.

non_functional.target: WCAG 2.1 AA — money-in distinction carries both a sign and colour; interactive links have accessible names; body-text contrast ≥4.5:1 in both light and dark themes

non_functional.why_not: No regulatory obligation attaches to a demo of a fictional bank with fictional data.

open_questions: AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9 and AC13 — the account detail page (app/accounts/[id]/page.tsx) does not exist today, so acceptance tests cannot import an entry point that would fail before the change and pass after. These criteria are checked by a component or e2e test added alongside the implementation, or by manual review (UMC-01).
AC10 — the 404 fall-through behaviour cannot be exercised via an existing entry point without the new dynamic route. Left to a route-level test added with the implementation (UMC-01).

AC11 — verifying the header appears on every page requires either extracting components/Header.tsx (which does not exist today) or rendering RootLayout inside jsdom (which is awkward with nested html/body). Left to a component-level test added with the extraction (UMC-01).

AC14 — the invariant 'each account has 10–15 transactions and balances reconcile' is naturally checked by a fixture test that reads data/accounts.json; that file does not exist today, so the test lands with the implementation (UMC-01).
AC15 — the changelog and RSS 'unchanged' criterion is a regression concern and would not fail before the change; the existing changelog test suite already covers it and no new test is added.
AC16 and AC17 — verifying no trademarked assets appear, and that a primary-blue CSS variable exists, is best done by manual review; automated checks would be brittle (UMC-01).
outcome: Visitors can view a fictional customer's three bank accounts and their recent transactions on the sandbox site, presented as a small internet-banking demo styled in deep blue.
rationale:
**Design shape.** One data file at `data/accounts.json` with nested transactions per account, mirroring `data/changelog.json`'s shape (one import, one source of truth, easy to keep the overview balance and newest-transaction balance in sync by hand). Slug-based ids ('everyday', 'savings', 'credit-card') for readable URLs and stable routing. A dynamic route `app/accounts/[id]/page.tsx` renders either the account or falls through to `app/not-found.tsx` via Next.js's `notFound()` helper. The header is extracted to `components/Header.tsx` and mounted inside `RootLayout` so it appears on every page; existing `ThemeToggle` and `Footer` are preserved. The deep-blue palette is expressed as CSS variables in `app/globals.css` and consumed via Tailwind classes; both light and dark modes get contrast-appropriate variants.

**Bank identity.** The user's suggestion was 'world bank or something generic'. The real World Bank Group exists, so a strictly-fictional generic name (Northline Bank) is used — this is trivial to change if a different name is preferred.

**Why no demo banner.** The user removed the demo-banner requirement from the original framing. The masked account numbers, absence of any password or PII prompt, and clearly fictional customer name are sufficient signals that this is not a real bank.

**Why signed amounts in one column.** Modern banking UIs use one signed amount column; it reads well on narrow screens and the sign carries meaning independently of colour (accessible).

**Why the credit card behaves like a spending account.** Consistency across the three accounts and one mental model of 'balance goes up with a debit, down with a credit'. The overview labels 'Owing' rather than 'Balance' for the credit card to make the sign convention unambiguous.

**Standards.** DTS-04 governs date rendering (DD MMM YYYY). SEC-01 §4 governs number masking (last four only). SEC-01 §3 governs the URL segment (whitelist match, not eval-like). PCP-02 forbids internal work-tracking refs in customer copy; the descriptions in the fixture must avoid any 'PAY-1234'-style references. DWR-01 does not apply — no writes.

**Test-coverage honesty.** The change creates new files (`data/accounts.json`, `app/accounts/[id]/page.tsx`, `components/Header.tsx`, several `lib/` helpers). Acceptance tests must import entry points that exist today, so most detail-page and header criteria fall into UMC-01: they are named and left uncovered by an executable test in this spec, to be covered by a component or e2e test added alongside the implementation. The home-page criteria (AC1–AC5, AC12) can and do have an acceptance test because `app/page.tsx` already exists.

1. Internal references must not be surfaced

swe_constraints: Preserve the anti-FOUC blocking script and ThemeProvider mounting order in app/layout.tsx; ThemeProvider must wrap all page content including the new Header.
The Header component must render inside RootLayout so it appears on every page including /changelog and the 404 page.

The existing Footer (components/Footer.tsx) continues to render below page content; the 'Last updated: DD MMM YYYY' behaviour is unchanged (may refactor its date formatter to the shared lib/formatDate.ts, but the rendered output must be identical).

The existing Changelog page (app/changelog/page.tsx), Changelog RSS route (app/changelog.xml/route.ts), ChangelogFilteredList and its filters must not be modified. Existing changelog tests must continue to pass without modification.
Dark mode is toggled via the .dark class on <html> (existing pattern) — do not introduce prefers-color-scheme media queries for theme switching.
No new NPM dependencies. Inline SVG icons (following components/ThemeToggle.tsx pattern) if any are needed.

The Next.js version is 16.2.6, which per AGENTS.md may differ from training data. Consult node_modules/next/dist/docs/ (App Router, dynamic routes, notFound()) before writing route or navigation code.
Account and card numbers in data/accounts.json store only the last four digits (e.g. '4821'); the full number is never present in the codebase or the DOM.
Account slug ids: 'everyday', 'savings', 'credit-card' — validate the URL param against this whitelist and call notFound() otherwise (SEC-01 §3).

The deep-blue palette must be a distinct choice — do not reproduce ANZ's specific hex codes, logo, or wordmark. A generic deep-blue family (e.g. Tailwind blue-700 / blue-800 for primary, adjusted for dark mode) is appropriate.
Money-in colour must have ≥4.5:1 contrast against the row background in both light and dark modes; do not rely on colour alone — the + / - sign carries the meaning.
HomePage (app/page.tsx) must remain a synchronous server component so it can be rendered directly in Jest via @testing-library/react.

Format money via Intl.NumberFormat with locale 'en-AU' and currency 'AUD' (or an equivalent template); always two decimal places; signed prefix '+' or '-' prepended manually so the sign appears outside the currency symbol (e.g. '-$45.00').
Transaction descriptions in data/accounts.json contain no internal work-tracking references such as 'PAY-1234' (PCP-02 §1).
